Historical Essay.

The question of the Municipal Regulations of the French
Concession, which was made one of the principal themes
by one of the candidates at the recent elections, is
a very important one and has already given rise to
a passionate controversy. We will, therefore, give a
short history of the Regulations.

The Role of the Consul in the Beginning.

Shanghai was declared an open port on November
17, 1843.
"Following upon the Treaty signed on October
24, 1844 by our Envoy Extraordinary and Minister
Plenipotentiary, Mr. Theodore de Lagrene," writes
Mr. Cordier in his "History of the Relations of
the Chinese with Occidental Powers, " we imitated
the example of the English and sent Mr. Montigny
as Consular Agent to Shanghai. We selected for
our concession the land from the shore of the
Whangpoo, between the Yangkingpang and the
walls of the Chinese city. The first Chinese
document which our interpreter considered as
constituting the first public act concerning
the French Concession in Shanghai is dated the
11th moon of the 28th year of Tao Kuang
(December 8, 1847------December 25, 1848); but
actually Taotai Lin signed the official
convention with Mr. Montigny on Friday, April 6, 1849."

The Consul then of necessity had a role of extreme
importance in all matters taking place in the Concession;
it was he, as representative of the nation, who had charge
of all diplomatic matters, and he it was also who signed
treaties, enforced them and interpreted their clauses.

科尔迪埃（Cordier）先生在其《中国与西方列强关系史》中写道：“继1844年10月24日我们的特命全权公使拉格勒内（Theodore de Lagrene）先生签署条约之后，我们效仿英国人的做法，派遣蒙蒂尼（Montigny）先生作为领事代理人前往上海。我们选取黄浦江岸、洋泾浜与中国城墙之间的土地作为我们的租界。我们的翻译认为构成关于上海法租界的第一份公共行为的第一份中文文件， dated 道光二十八年十一月十一日（1847年12月8日------1848年12月25日）；但实际上，道台林是在1849年4月6日星期五与蒙蒂尼先生签署正式协定的。”

因此，领事在租界发生的所有事务中必然扮演着极其重要的角色；作为国家代表，他负责所有外交事务，也是他签署条约、执行条约并解释其条款。这并不是一个容易扮演的角色。我们在下文附上中国海关的福韦尔（Fauvel）先生对蒙蒂尼先生的评论：
“德·蒙蒂尼先生于1847年11月乘坐一艘英国商船抵达上海。从次年8月起，我们发现他忙于从中国当局那里获得购买土地的许可，以便为第一位在上海定居的法国商人建造房屋和商店。这位商人是雷米（Remy）先生，他娶了蒙蒂尼先生的女儿，后来改名为雷米-蒙蒂尼（Remy-Montigny）。他还利用雷米先生的这一要求，向道台沈辉（Sam Hoo，音译，苏松太道）主张为法国划设一块租界。在他于1848年8月20日从上海发给部长的第19号公文中，他说：
‘我已亲自选定了地块位置，并将其指明为最便于经商的地方；它比英租界更靠近城市，且在

Mr. de Montigny was far from the end of his
worries, for no sooner had he issued a proclamation
the demand for a concession that the American Consular
Agent, Mr. Griswold, who represented in Shanghai the
firm of Russel and Co., learning of it through the

departments of Soochow, Sungkiang and Taitang, in the

against our claim for a concession.

As one could see the diplomatic negotiations
of the Consul was a heavy task. His role did not end
at that: he had frequently to intervene in all private
matters of that period.

For instance, if it was easy to indicate on paper
the territory in which Europeans may habitate, it was
not so easy to take possession. The land on which a
merchant desired to construct his hong or his residence
belonged to owners who had first of all to be dispossessed;
these latter did their best, with the backing of the
mandarins, to prolong the negotiations as much as possible,
and even without this support, they would have, through
avarice, tried to secure as high a price as possible.
The merchant, not being able to secure possession of the
land, naturally turned to the Consul, in whose person
were represented the power of the law, and also, it ought
to be said, the soldiers before whom the mandarins had
eventually to give way.

Mr. Montalto de Jesus, in his "Historic Shanghai,"
writes as follows:-
"Before the smallest piece of land could
be acquired, long and harassing parleys
usually take place between the Consul and the
merchants on the one part and the mandarins
and the land owners on the other. The
difficulties do not cease with the dispossession
of the landowners for they would refuse to quit
under the smallest pretext, and when they
finish by eventually going away they will leave
behind in their place an old woman (a shrew)

商店前面，有一条可供舢板和大型驳船航行的小河汊；因此我们的同胞将得到良好的供应，无可抱怨。此事不会引起任何困难，我希望在几天内能在华北拥有两家法国商行，巴克、阿尔屈埃公司（Bac, Arcue et Cie.）已表示希望在法租界设立机构。’”

这就解释了为何出于避免与中国人发生冲突的愿望——正如英国人试图购买位于其租界内的中国房屋时所发生的那样——有必要确保支付金额不超过土地价值，正如8月6日正式提出租界要求之日所确定的那样。这一点可以从与官员们往来的大量信函中看出，科尔迪埃先生提供了这些信函的译文，从中我们注意到，我们的领事不得不等待六个月，直到1849年3月20日，而不是他所提到的几天。

德·蒙蒂尼先生的烦恼远未结束，因为他刚一发布关于租界要求的公告，代表罗素公司（Russel and Co.）在上海的美国领事代理人格里斯沃尔德（Griswold）先生，通过江苏省苏州、松江和太仓兵备道道台林于1849年4月6日发布的公告得知此事后，便写信抗议我们对租界的主张。

由此可见，领事的外交谈判是一项繁重的任务。他的角色并未就此结束：他经常不得不干预当时的所有私人事务。

例如，如果在纸上划定欧洲人可以居住的区域很容易，那么实际占有就不那么容易了。商人希望在其上建造商行或住宅的土地属于需要先被剥夺所有权的业主；这些业主在官员的支持下，极力尽可能延长谈判时间，即使没有这种支持，他们也会出于贪婪，试图争取尽可能高的价格。商人既然无法获得土地占有权，自然转向领事，因为领事代表着法律的权力，而且应该说，还代表着最终迫使官员让步的士兵。

蒙塔尔托·德·耶稣（Montalto de Jesus）先生在其《上海史》中写道：
“在能够 acquiring 最小的一块土地之前，领事和商人一方与官员和土地所有者另一方之间通常会发生漫长而令人烦恼的谈判。困难并不随着土地所有者被剥夺所有权而停止，因为他们会以最小的借口拒绝离开，而当他们最终离开时，他们会留下一个老妇人（泼妇）

except that of money. These old viragos
were thus able to make money either in
a purchase or sale of land. If they are
injured they retaliate with great violence,
if one touches them they lament until one

if the Consul comes along with the

In short, the acquisition of land in the

Says Mr. Fauvel:-
"For the purchase of anything in the
French Concession, bargaining takes place
article by article with the Taotai, the
owners demanding in effect exhorbitant
sums, 100% more than what was paid by the
Consul."

Mr. Montigny had selected a difficult lot of
land; it was covered with houses and the Consul
encountered innumerable difficulties in the process
of dispossession.
To acquire land is not sufficient in itself:
one must live there, conduct business and be in
touch with the Chinese. The Consul had therefore
to step in again and specify the rights and the
obligations of the Europeans, and what those of
the Chinese should be. He must also decide, in
co-operation with the Chinese authorities, what
articles of commerce the Europeans may trade in,
what kind of buildings they may construct (churches,
dwelling houses or shops), stipulate the things
which are forbidden to both foreigners and Chinese
(prohibition of the use of firearms in order not
to frighten the Chinese inhabitants, and the
prohibition of Chinese to reside in the French
Concession), to regulate the removal of graves,
a very delicate matter liable to give rise to
rioting, as happened 30 years later in the affair
of the Ningpo Cemetery Guild Cemetery. All these
things could be undertaken only by the Consul.
For at this time the French Consuls had not
only to deal with the other foreign consuls and
the Chinese authorities ----for it must be said that
it was due to them that we are able to have our
Concession to-day despite the advice of the English
and American consuls----but he had also to appear
in person to protect his nationals. We read
with interest, for example, in the "History of the
Kiangnan Mission," how Mr. Montigny, accompanied
only by his secretary, Count Kleckowski,
proceeded to Sikawei where a band of pillagers
was menacing the place threatening to burn and
destroy it. Accompanied by the Paotseng, he
went to the place where the band had assembled and
found over one hundred of them gathered together,
and through his sang-froid he dispersed them.
Once Mr. Montigny learnt that a number of shipwrecked
French sailors were held in captivity in Korea. He went
there in a lorcha and rescued them, and returned them
to Shanghai.

福韦尔先生说：
“在法租界购买任何东西，都要与道台逐项讨价还价，业主实际上索要巨额款项，比领事支付的金额高出100%。”

蒙蒂尼先生选中了一块难啃的地皮；上面覆盖着房屋，领事在剥夺所有权的过程中遇到了无数困难。
仅仅获得土地是不够的：人们必须在那里生活、做生意并与中国人保持联系。因此，领事不得不再次介入，明确规定欧洲人的权利和义务，以及中国人的权利和义务。他还必须与中国当局合作，决定欧洲人可以交易哪些商品，可以建造哪种类型的建筑物（教堂、住宅或商店），规定禁止外国人和中国人做的事情（禁止使用枪支以免惊吓中国居民，以及禁止中国人居住在法租界），规范坟墓迁移，这是一件非常微妙的事情，容易引发骚乱，正如30年后在宁波公墓公会墓地事件中发生的那样。所有这些事务只能由领事来处理。因为当时法国领事不仅要与其他外国领事和中国当局打交道——必须指出，尽管有英国和美国领事的建议，正是由于他们的努力，我们今天才能拥有这块租界——他还必须亲自出面保护本国国民。例如，我们在《江南传教史》中饶有兴趣地读到，蒙蒂尼先生仅由其秘书克莱茨科夫斯基（Kleckowski）伯爵陪同，前往徐家汇，那里有一群掠夺者正威胁要焚烧和摧毁该地。他在保正（Paotseng，音译）的陪同下，前往匪徒聚集的地方，发现有一百多人聚集在一起，他凭借冷静沉着将他们驱散。有一次，蒙蒂尼先生得知一批遇难的法国水手被扣押在朝鲜。他乘坐一艘 Lorcha（中式帆船）前往那里，解救了他们，并将他们带回上海。

From the Echo de Chine of January 25, 1923.

Establishment of the first Municipalities.
From Nov. 29, 1845 two years after the opening of the Port, the British Consul Mr. Balfour, in agreement with Taotai Kung, drew up the first Municipal charter which was to regulate the administration of the British Concession. He placed the internal administration in the hands of the land owners. The latter, as a united body were responsible for the good maintenance of the Concession and had to furnish the funds which were to be used for its maintenance. It must, however, be remarked that it was the Consul who, on his own authority, named the first land commission for the purpose of determining the amount of contribution that each individual was to furnish.
In the French Concession it was not until 1862 that the Consul instituted a Municipal Commission.
No surprise ought to be occasioned at the fact that this institution was begun so late. The main cause of this delay is to be found in the fact that there were very few French citizens in the Concession, for with the exception of missionaries there was but one French house in Shanghai, that belonging to M.Roni, who succeeded in acquiring land loud thanks to the efforts of M.De Montigny, at the beginning of 1849.
M. Hontalto of Jesus writes :- "The French Concession remained quite neglected and for years one could only see the Consulate (a Chinese home) and the establishment of a merchant dealing in Parisian watches".

A little digression here to show that no reproach should be attached to M. de Montigny that French trade was not more flourishing.
"It is not M. de Montigny's fault", writes the Rev. Father Basillion, in his history of the Kiangnan Mission from 1842 to 1855, "if our country did not draw of its good will the material profits which, in determining the nature of its protection - (he writes these lines in 1855-55)- would strengthen her moral authority. The commerce of France lacked initiative. It did not decide to woo fortune in the foot steps of the British or American wealthy societies. In order to interest France in Chinese trade, the French Consulate, thought of opening markets for her factories and of facilitating an importing trade through barter between her and China. Hence the investigations, the sending of linen, silk, tobacco, animals, etc. Why is it that amongst the flags which float side by side with the three thousand Chinese junks, the colors of our merchant marine have only appeared on the Whangpoo three or four times on ordinary occasions?"
And further more "If there have not yet been substantial transactions between the French and the large firms of Shanghai and Soochow, it is because our compatriots did not know how to take advantage of the advances which were made to them. An order for three millions amongst others, was addressed to the French Consulate for our merchants. This order was given according to samples and every possible guarantee was offered. M. de Montigny had the chagrin to see the fruits of his zeal pass by. It is not long ago that the French Consul in Shanghai had again to make use of a British firm for an order of from two to three hundred thousand francs of French products".
Here is something said in praise of M.de Montigny by M. Ernest Millot at a conference given by him at a session of the Assembly of the Indo-Chinese Academy in 1881 : "Since his

首批市政机构的建立。
从1845年11月29日，即开埠两年后，英国领事巴尔福（Balfour）先生与龚道台协商，制定了第一部市政章程，以规范英租界的行政管理。他将内部管理权交给土地所有者。后者作为一个整体，负责租界的良好维护，并必须提供用于维护的资金。然而，必须指出的是，是第一任土地委员会由领事凭其职权任命，目的是确定每个人应缴纳的捐款数额。
在法租界，直到1862年，领事才设立了市政委员会。
这一机构起步如此之晚，并不令人惊讶。造成这种延误的主要原因在于，租界内的法国公民极少，因为除了传教士外，上海只有一家法国商行，即罗尼（Roni，音译）先生的商行，他得益于德·蒙蒂尼先生的努力，在1849年初成功获得了土地。
Hontalto of Jesus（原文如此，应为Montalto de Jesus）先生写道：“法租界一直备受冷落，多年来人们只能看到领事馆（一所中式住宅）和一家经营巴黎钟表的商人的店铺”。

在此稍作插叙，以表明不应因法国贸易不够繁荣而指责德·蒙蒂尼先生。
巴斯利翁（Basillion）神父在其《1842年至1855年江南传教史》中写道：“如果我们的国家没有从其善意中获得物质利益——他在1855年写下这些文字——从而加强其道德权威，这并非德·蒙蒂尼先生的过错。法国商业缺乏主动性。它没有决定追随英美富商群体的脚步去追求财富。为了使法国对中国贸易产生兴趣，法国领事馆想到了为其工厂打开市场，并通过与中国进行易货贸易来促进进口贸易。因此进行了调查，发送了亚麻布、丝绸、烟草、动物等。为什么在与三千艘中国舢板并列飘扬的旗帜中，我们的商船队的颜色在平常情况下只在黄浦江上出现过三四次？”
此外，“如果法国人与上海和苏州的大商行之间尚未进行实质性的交易，那是因为我们的同胞不知道如何利用向他们提供的机会。其中有一份价值三百万的订单发给了法国领事馆，供我们的商人承接。这份订单是根据样品下达的，并提供了所有可能的保证。德·蒙蒂尼先生遗憾地看着他的热情成果付诸东流。不久之前，上海法国领事不得不再次通过一家英国商行来处理一笔价值两三十万法郎的法国产品订单”。
以下是欧内斯特·米洛（Ernest Millot）先生在1881年印度支那学院会议的一次演讲中对德·蒙蒂尼先生的赞扬：“自从他

It must be said in exoneration of our merchants that

not precisely such that would induce them to come and establish

Shanghai, April 7, 1853.
"Monsieur le Superior,
The gravity of the situation and especially the rapid

In short only the French offered their assistance to

抵达上海后，在1847年的最后几个月里，他向外交部提交了关于加那利群岛（?Islands）贸易以及马来西亚和印度支那产品的精辟报告。这些文件附上了茶叶、木材、古塔波胶（gutta-percha）、淀粉和植物的样本，孟提尼先生（M.de Montigny）认为这些植物可以在阿尔及利亚或法国种植。同时，他还向法国各城镇的商会提交了关于中国物资的报告。在一份 dated 1848年6月25日的报告中，他说：“我在上海绝对有必要设立一个永久性的展览，让中国商人可以经常前来研究我们工业的产品，并计算提供给他们的优势。”

与此同时，他在各个地点建立法国代理人，组织了一支悬挂法国国旗的中国帆船船队，每艘船由一名法国水手担任船长，以维持上海与宁波之间的沿海服务；修订海关税则，使其在宁波的管辖权得到承认；忙于为法国人建立专用墓地；并从1847年至1854年，从未停止向外交部发送关于满洲、蒙古和直隶的商业、中国渔业以及瓷器制造的笔记。

必须为我们的商人说句公道话，当时中国特别是上海周边的局势，并不足以促使他们来到黄浦江畔定居。太平天国起义于1850年底爆发。被称为“红党”的反叛者与太平军结盟或假装结盟，并于1853年初威胁上海。孟提尼先生认为局势已足够严重，致信耶稣会传教士团负责人布鲁永神父（Father Brouillon），信件内容如下：

上海，1853年4月7日。
“尊敬的院长先生：

the Reds lasted less than 17 months.
A few years later, the Taipings themselves came up
to the city walls. On June 29, 1860 Soochow was taken by
them and in August they proceeded towards Shanghai.
We shall not here enter into the history of the battles
which took place around Shanghai, suffice it to say that
they lasted about three years. What we have just said
will sufficiently show that those various agitations were
not made to encourage the French to come and install them-
selves in our Concession, exposed always to the first attacks.

M. Huissonnet, whose name will be mentioned further
in the course of this history in his introduction to a
narration which he made of his travels from Peking to Shanghai,
seems to have referred only to the serious relations between
the European Powers and China after the Franco-British
expedition of 1860.
It always happens after such expeditions that certain
mere adventurers upon the termination of a war, would estab-
lish themselves in the countries where they are able to
know the inhabitants and where they see opportunities of making
a fortune more rapidly. It is thus, we think, that the
coming of the first French merchants to our Concession may
be explained. There was already a large number of Chinese
as all the uprisings which had taken place viz : that of the
Reds in 1854, the Taipings in 1860 resulted in drawing
to Concessions a large number of refugees, who came to seek
protection under foreign guns. Chinese merchants eager to
deal in smuggling especially contraband of war at the period
and who could more easily meddle with foreigners in their
own concessions did not fail to come and install themselves
with us; our concession offered them the advantage of being
nearer to walls of the Chinese city, an advantage which
attracted them.
In short our concession in 1860 contained also a
certain number of British and American merchants who were
led to do so by the prospect of easier relations with the
Chinese. What then could have been the total of the popu-
lation in the French Concession ? In 1865 it seems according
to figures given by Montalto de Jesus that the Chinese
already numbered 50,000 persons and foreigners about 400.
The figures are certainly exaggerated. In a pamphlet by
M. Millot former President of the Council, a letter written
by several French merchants in 1880-82 gave the following
figures which cannot be disputed : "The French Concession
of Shanghai, China, contains 500 Europeans and 33,000
Chinese and has a Municipal budget of 700,000 Francs".
Would it be exaggerating to think that the Concession towards
1863 could at least be reckoned at a hundred European mer-
chants of whom fifteen were French, and fifteen thousand
Chinese ?
The enormous disproportion between Foreigners and
Chinese is remarkable. It can be imagined that the duties
of those then in power had reference especially to Police
questions and it is also one of the reasons why the entire
administration of the concession had remained for so long
a time in the hands of the Consul above.

“红党”占领的时间不到17个月。

几年后，太平军本身逼近城墙。1860年6月29日，苏州被他们攻占，8月他们向上海进发。

我们在此不赘述上海周围发生的战斗历史， suffice it to say that 它们持续了大约三年。我们刚才所说的足以表明，这些各种动荡并没有鼓励法国人来我们的租界定居，因为这里总是首当其冲受到攻击。

惠松内先生（M. Huissonnet），他的名字将在本历史叙述中进一步提及，在他关于从北京到上海旅行的叙述引言中，似乎仅提到了1860年英法远征之后欧洲列强与中国之间的严肃关系。

在这样的远征之后，总有一些纯粹的冒险者在战争结束时，定居在他们能够了解居民并看到更快发财机会的国家。我们认为，第一批法国商人来到我们租界的原因或许可以由此解释。当时已有大量中国人，因为所有发生的起义，即：1854年的“红党”起义和1860年的太平天国起义，导致大量难民涌入租界，寻求外国炮火的保护。急于从事走私贸易、特别是战时违禁品贸易的中国商人，以及那些更容易在自己的租界内与外国人打交道的人，纷纷前来并在我们这里定居；我们的租界为他们提供了靠近中国城墙的优势，这一优势吸引了他们。

总之，1860年我们的租界也包含一定数量的英国和美国商人，他们是出于与中国人建立更轻松关系的展望而被吸引来的。那么，法租界的人口总数是多少呢？根据蒙塔尔托·德·耶稣（Montalto de Jesus）提供的数据，1865年中国人似乎已达50,000人，外国人约400人。这些数字肯定被夸大了。在前公董局主席米洛先生（M. Millot）的一本小册子中，一封由几位法国商人在1880-82年间写的信给出了以下无可争议的数字：“中国上海法租界拥有500名欧洲人和33,000名中国人，市政预算为700,000法郎”。如果认为1863年左右租界至少可估算为有一百名欧洲商人（其中十五名为法国人）和一万五千名中国人，这算是夸大吗？

外国人与中国人之间的巨大比例失调是显著的。可以想象，当时掌权者的职责尤其涉及警务问题，这也是整个租界行政长期掌握在上述领事手中的原因之一。

From the Echo de Chine of January 26, 1923.

II. Establishment of the first Municipalities.
It would be more accurate from the historical point
of view, to say that the French Concession from 1854 had a
Municipal regime in common with other concessions. It was
in that year in fact that the land regulations were revised
and sanctioned by the Powers in agreement with China.
There was formed", says Mr. Fauvel, " a General Munici-
pal Council. The members of the Council were to be named by
all land owners regardless of nationality".
In practice, however, the French Concession found itself
a little placed on the shelf by the Municipal Council com-
posed of several Americans and a majority of English. We
could not, with the small number of French firms, then of
little importance commercially, obtrude upon the powerful
hongs of the English and Americans, who at that time were
having very good business in tea, silk and opium.
The meetings of the Municipal Council at the time clear-
ly show that the two Concessions viz: the English and the
American, were the special object of their solicitude. This
fact naturally led our Consuls to endeavour the establishing
of a separate French Municipality as soon as there was a
sufficient number of French people. Mr. Edan of the
considered that moment had arrived in 1862.
Mr. Mac Lellan in his history of Shanghai says: "The
land owners were called to a General meeting on April 30,
1862 and the Consul designated five members, all of whom
were Frenchmen, to constitute the first Council for the Ad-
ministration of the French Concession. They agreed to com-
mence their duties from May 1, and on the 9th of the same
month they held a meeting. Every year a general meeting of
land owners was to be held".
Mr. Edan communicated the news to Mr. Medhurst, the
English Consul, in the following letter:-
"Sir, I have the honour to inform you that I have es-
tablished a Municipal Council, empowered by means of
certain general contributions towards the expenditure
which may be necessary for the Police, the breaking up
and the upkeep of roads and in general for everything
that is for the public welfare in the French Concession.
The members of the Council are: Messrs. A. Buissonnet,
Chairman, H. Moynard, E.C. Fajard, T. Marriquet, Ed.
Schmidt, Treasurer and Secretary.
This establishment was urgently demanded by the needs
of both the native and European population, which had
increased enormously of late and is destined to bring
about a new and effective co-operation in the work of
maintaining order, sanitation and security in Shanghai.
Moreover I do not doubt, Sir, that the utmost
harmony which we desire to see established will prevail
in the relations of our two Municipal Corporations, which
have the same task to fulfill and the same object in
view, though on different land".
Mr. Medhurst, in a letter which he wrote to the English
Municipal Council, admitted the advantages which the forma-
tion of this new Council would bring; he, however, mentioned
the question of its legality, declaring that this measure
was entirely in opposition to the Shanghai Land Regulations
as approved by the Powers in treaties. One would surmise that
he would not care to accept the fact of any independent French
Concession. The Municipal Council of the International Set-

二、首批市政机构的建立。
从历史角度来看，更准确的说法是，法租界自1854年起与其他租界共同拥有市政制度。事实上，正是在那一年，土地章程经过修订，并由列强与中国共同批准。福韦尔先生（Mr. Fauvel）说：“成立了一个通用工部局（General Municipal Council）。委员会成员应由所有土地所有者提名，不论其国籍如何”。

然而，在实践中，法租界发现自己被一个由几名美国人和多数英国人组成的工部局略微搁置一旁。凭借当时数量稀少且商业影响力不大的法国商行，我们无法强行介入势力强大的英美洋行，后者当时在茶叶、丝绸和鸦片生意上做得非常好。

当时的工部局会议清楚地表明，两个租界，即英租界和美租界，是他们特别关注的对象。这一事实自然促使我们的领事努力在法国人数量足够时建立一个独立的法国市政机构。艾丹先生（Mr. Edan）认为这一时刻在1862年已经到来。

麦克莱伦先生（Mr. Mac Lellan）在他的《上海史》中说：“土地所有者于1862年4月30日被召集参加全体会议，领事指定五名成员，均为法国人，组成法租界行政管理的第一届委员会。他们同意从5月1日开始履行职责，并于同月9日举行了会议。每年将举行一次土地所有者全体会议”。

艾丹先生在以下信函中将此消息通知了英国领事麦华陀先生（Mr. Medhurst）：

“先生，我很荣幸地通知您，我已成立了一个市政委员会，有权通过某些普遍捐款来支付可能需要的开支，用于警务、道路的修建和维护，以及总体上用于法租界内一切关乎公共福利的事务。委员会成员为：A. 布伊松内特先生（A. Buissonnet，主席）、H. 穆瓦纳尔先生（H. Moynard）、E.C. 法亚尔先生（E.C. Fajard）、T. 马里凯特先生（T. Marriquet）、埃德·施密特先生（Ed. Schmidt，财务兼秘书）。

这一机构的建立是本地人口和欧洲人口的迫切需求，近期这两类人口均大幅增长，注定将为维护上海的秩序、卫生和安全工作带来新的有效合作。此外，先生，我毫不怀疑，我们希望看到的最大和谐将盛行于我们两个市政机构之间的关系中，尽管位于不同的土地上，但它们肩负着相同的任务，有着相同的目标。”

麦华陀先生在写给英国工部局的信中，承认了这个新委员会的成立所带来的好处；然而，他提到了其合法性问题，声明这一措施完全违背了经条约批准列强认可的《上海土地章程》。人们可能会推测，他不愿意接受任何独立的法租界存在的事实。公共租界工部局……

The first notes which we find on the subject of the
French Municipal Council's works are in the issue of
North China Herald of May 2, 1863. They were reported
on the occasion of the first meeting held by the land
owners charged to approve the work already done and to
determine a budget for the next year.
It is well to note that this meeting was held at the
French General Consulate and that it was Mr. Mauboussin,
the Consul, who presided. He was the first speaker. He
said:-
"The Council having lost one of its members, I had
to think of his successor. Mr. Baron seemed to me to pos-
sess all the qualities necessary for a member of the Mu-
nicipal Council. I feel convinced beforehand that this
nomination will meet with no objection on your part.
Now as regards the future. Very important interests
are attached to the lot of this Concession and everything
concerning its administration, and I deem it my duty, in
order to safeguard my responsibility to call the attention
of my Government to the actual situation here and to ask
for instructions. My plan is to get enlightenment on the fol-
lowing question. The Imperial Government desires a strict
observance of the treaties and as protector of this Con-
cession has the right to give its opinion on all changes
which may interest it: will the Government leave the Coun-
cil free to select alone as before, the persons willing
to help in the maintenance of the Police and good order?
Or else, taking into consideration the numerous foreign
interests mixed with those of its nationals, will the
Government prefer to let the meeting of ratepayers help
in the choice of a Council by their advice and voting?
For my part, I must inform you, that I am in favour of
the latter and intend to submit a general draft of the
Municipal Regulations to the Department for Foreign Affairs
The Council, in presenting a report of its work, pro-
nounced the following significant phrase: " Arrived at
the end of our first year of management, we have requested
the Consul General to convene the Council in order that
we may render you an account for the past year".
Nothing could be more clear than these documents to
define the role of the Consul vis-a-vis the Municipal
Council. He by right named the first Council. A replace-
ment being required during the year, his choice falls upon
Mr. Baron and he presents him for approval to the meeting
of land owners. Mr. Mauboussin declares clearly that up
to the present the Consul only could select the Council,
and if he asks for more liberal instructions from Paris,
he reserves to himself the right to choose Councillors
who will have to be approved by the ratepayers. The land
owners' meeting, which is presided over by the Consul, is
held in the Consulate, and if it takes place, it is at
the request of the Council to the Consul General.

"At present it seems that members of the Council are named

individual whom he has selected will consent to act as

render all ratepayers eligible for election to the Council

我们发现的关于法公董局工程事项的最早记录，见于1863年5月2日出版的《北华捷报》。这些报道出现在土地所有者召开的首次会议上，该会议旨在批准已完成的工程并确定下一年度的预算。

值得注意的是，这次会议是在法国总领事馆举行的，由领事莫布桑（Mauboussin）先生主持。他是第一位发言者。他说：

“公董局失去了一名成员，我不得不考虑其继任者。巴伦（Baron）先生在我看来具备担任公董局成员所需的一切素质。我深信这一提名不会遭到各位的反对。

现在谈谈未来。本租界的命运及其行政管理涉及极其重要的利益，我认为我有责任提请本国政府注意这里的实际情况并请求指示，以维护我的责任。我的计划是就以下问题寻求澄清。帝国政府希望严格遵守条约，作为本租界的保护者，有权对任何可能涉及其利益的变化发表意见：政府是否会让公董局像以前一样，独自自由选择愿意协助维持警务和良好秩序的人员？或者，考虑到与其国民利益交织在一起的众多外国利益，政府是否更倾向于让纳税人会议通过建议和投票来协助选择公董局成员？就我而言，我必须告知各位，我赞成后者，并打算向外交部提交一份《市政章程》的总体草案。”

公董局在提交其工作报告时，发表了如下意味深长的言论：“在我们管理的第一年结束时，我们已请求总领事召集公董局，以便我们就过去一年的工作向各位汇报。”

这些文件对于界定领事相对于公董局的角色再清楚不过了。他依职权任命了第一届公董局。年内需要补缺时，他选择了巴伦先生，并将其提交给土地所有者会议批准。莫布桑先生明确表示，迄今为止只有领事可以选拔公董局成员，如果他向巴黎请求更自由的指示，他保留选择须经纳税人批准的董事的权利。由领事主持的土地所有者会议在领事馆举行，如果召开此类会议，也是应公董局向总领事的请求而进行的。

《北华捷报》在报道这次会议时写道：“目前看来，公董局成员由领事任命，领事只关心他所选定的人是否同意担任董事。无论如何，莫布桑先生已宣布，他打算向本国政府提交一项计划，使所有纳税人都具备当选为公董局成员的资格。”

The question of the respective positions of the
Consul and the Council was undoubtedly the subject of dis-
cussion by our predecessors: one had to await with a cer-
tain amount of patience the instructions to come from
France and the decisions in favour of a very liberal re-
gulation had to be as strong as possible because there
was before us the example of the neighbouring Concession
and because the French Concession contained a large num-
ber of land owners. Relations between the French and the
Foreigners were very consistent and even very cordial at
that time. "At the outset" remarks Mr. Buissonnet, "na-
tionality and special interests caused no discord; on the
contrary there was perfect understanding and Shanghai was
justly entitled a model colony".
With the French, the question that seemed mostly to
occupy their minds, was that of the quality of the electors.
Would the land owners be always the only ones to vote and
would the hong employees be for ever deprived of this vote?
The following letter written in French by a French-
man and signed "Equality" is to be found in the "North Chi-
na Herald" of April 23, 1864: "The question is to revive
the French Municipal Commission. Already as it was done
two years ago, the list of real estate owners, who alone
may nominate the five or six members of this Commission,
is being prepared. In 1862 when the Municipal Commission
was instituted the Consul in fact consulted the land
owners only, this was a temporary but dictatory measure
it is true, but one that could be justified by circumstan-
ces at that time. To-day this measure will not hold good.
After recalling that "the principle that vivifies,
animates and dominates all our laws and our institutions"
is that " the one who votes and spends the tax must be
elected by the one who pays it," the writer advocates that
besides the land owners, all European residents paying
taxes should be sent for election "in such a manner that the
interests of everybody would be safeguarded and municipal
decisions would have lawful force".
He incidentally refers to the Commission's func-
tions: "these functions, after having been formerly sanc-
tioned by the authorities and the privileged class of pro-
prietors, should in future be confirmed by a full mandate
of all fellow citizens". It would in fact be a liberal
proposition and the attribution of power by the mandate
of the people.
The "North China Herald" unfortunately did not pub-
lish an account of the general meeting of ratepayers held
in the year 1864 ; it only gave extracts of the reports
on the municipal administration.
But we are already nearing the famous crisis of
1865 which precipitated matters.

留将自己选定的人选提交给纳税人投票的权利。

领事与公董局各自的地位问题无疑曾是我们前任们讨论的主题：人们必须带着一定的耐心等待来自法国的指示，而支持非常自由化的规章制度的决定必须尽可能有力，因为摆在我们面前的是邻近租界的先例，而且法租界拥有大量的土地所有者。当时法国人与外国人之间的关系非常一致，甚至非常融洽。“起初，”布伊索内（Buissonnet）先生 remarked，“国籍和特殊利益并未引起不和；相反，大家有着完美的理解，上海被公正地称为模范殖民地”。

对于法国人来说，似乎最让他们挂心的问题是选举人的资格问题。土地所有者是否会永远是唯一的投票者？洋行雇员是否将永远被剥夺这一投票权？

一封由一名法国人用法文撰写并署名“平等”（Equality）的信刊登在1864年4月23日的《北华捷报》上：“问题在于恢复法国市政委员会。就像两年前所做的那样，正在编制一份房地产所有者名单，只有他们才能提名该委员会的五六名成员。1862年设立市政委员会时，领事实际上只咨询了土地所有者，这确实是一项临时但独断的措施，但在当时的情况下是可以证明其合理性的。今天，这项措施已不再适用。”

在回顾“赋予我们要法律和我们机构以生机、活力并主导一切的原则”是“投票和花费税款的人必须由缴纳税款的人选出”之后，作者主张除了土地所有者外，所有缴纳税款的欧洲居民都应参与选举，“以此方式，每个人的利益都将得到保障，市政决策将具有合法效力”。

他顺便提到了委员会的职能：“这些职能以前曾得到当局和特权阶层业主的认可，今后应由全体同胞的完整授权予以确认。”这实际上是一项自由化的提议，即通过人民的授权来赋予权力。

遗憾的是，《北华捷报》并未刊登1864年举行的纳税人大会的记录；它只刊登了有关市政管理的报告摘录。

但我们已经接近著名的1865年危机，这场危机加速了事态的发展。

III. The Crisis of 1865.
In 1876 Mr. Brenier de Montmorand arrived in Peking as Minister of France. A phrase which often flowed from his pen was: "it is not necessary to have an excess of zeal", and that "prudent forms, measures and precautions should be taken". He advised "the avoidance of all pretext to initiate", and never ceased to demand of the people "to exercise the greatest prudence, the greatest reserve". Had his age imparted him wisdom? Or was it rather that, being punctilious of his rights and prerogatives, he had been much less so where it concerned others? His conduct in 1865 in any case contradicted in an absolute manner the advice that he gave out a dozen years later.
He arrived in Shanghai in 1864. Did the councillors wish to take advantage of the inexperience of a newly arrived Consul to enlarge their powers or had Brenier de Montmorand made himself too abrupt at the start?
At any rate the relations between the two became rapidly strained, for, a year after the arrival of Brenier de Montmorand, we see the Council rejecting all attempts at reconciliation and the Consul on his side made use immediately of brutal force.

On October 3, 1865 the Municipal Council gave orders directly to the local Police, the Consul, having been immediately informed of the measure which had been taken, sent on the 4th a letter to the Council, requesting it to be good enough to revoke a portion of the instructions which it had given and to come to an understanding with the Consul who was alone responsible to Foreign and Chinese authorities and to his own Government.
The Council did not reply to this letter and invited by a notice which appeared in the "North China Herald" on October 14, but already signed on the 7th by the secretary of Municipal Council, the land owners of the Concession to attend a special general meeting to be held on October 1st at the Municipal Hall.
The Consul replied by an order dated October 12 dissolving the Council, closing the Municipal Hall, and in a notice of the same date requested the land owners to meet at the French Consulate on the same date and at the same hour as that fixed by the Council, but with the venue at the French General Consulate.
The "North China Herald" does not give an account of these two meetings, whether the one convened by the Councillors did at all take place; but it seems that the Councillors were not followed in the path into which they wished to lead the land owners of the Concession. The reasons given by the Consul in his order show well, it seems to us, that the Councillors had committed an abuse of power and very few persons could have wished to support them.
The answer given by the Councillors was of little force it replied to the accusation made against their management, but it was in a vague manner that it refuted the arguments of the Consul on the subject of the authority which belonged to him by established custom, to name councillors directly.
A discussion of this took place in the Council itself, otherwise how could it be explained that Mr. Buissonnet, who was Chairman of the Council, acted as member of the Municipal Commission which is named by Consular authority?

三、1865年危机。

1876年，布雷尼埃·德·蒙莫朗（Brenier de Montmorand）先生以法国公使身份抵达北京。他笔下常流出的一句话是：“不必有过度的热情”，以及“应采取谨慎的形式、措施和预防手段”。他建议“避免任何发起行动的借口”，并不断要求人们“行使最大的谨慎，保持最大的克制”。是他的年龄赋予了他智慧吗？还是说，因为他对自己的权利和特权一丝不苟，而在涉及他人时却远非如此？无论如何，他在1865年的行为与他十多年后提出的建议绝对矛盾。

他于1864年抵达上海。董事们是否想利用一位新到任领事的经验不足来扩大他们的权力，还是布雷尼埃·德·蒙莫朗一开始就表现得过于生硬？

不管怎样，双方关系迅速紧张起来，因为在布雷尼埃·德·蒙莫朗到达一年后，我们看到公董局拒绝了所有和解尝试，而领事方面则立即使用了粗暴的武力。

1865年10月3日，公董局直接向当地警察下达命令，领事在得知所采取的措施后立即于4日致信公董局，请其撤销已发出的部分指令，并与领事达成共识，因为只有领事才对中外当局及其本国政府负责。

公董局未回复此信，而是通过10月14日刊登在《北华捷报》上、但已于7日由公董局秘书签署的通知，邀请租界土地所有者参加定于10月1日在工部局大厅举行的特别大会。

领事则以10月12日发布的命令作为回应，解散公董局，关闭工部局大厅，并在同日的一份通知中，要求土地所有者在与公董局规定的相同日期和相同时间集会，但地点改为法国总领事馆。

《北华捷报》未对这两次会议进行报道，由董事们召集的那次会议是否真正召开也不得而知；但似乎董事们并未得到他们试图引导的租界土地所有者的追随。领事在其命令中给出的理由充分表明，在我们看来，董事们滥用了权力，很少有人愿意支持他们。

董事们的答复力度不大，虽然回应了针对其管理的指控，但对于领事关于其依据既定惯例拥有直接任命董事权力的论点，其反驳含糊其辞。

此事甚至在公董局内部也引发了讨论，否则如何解释身为公董局主席的布伊索内先生，竟然 acting as 由领事权威任命的市政委员会的成员呢？

剩下的四位董事发现自己被孤立了，而我们的观点得到证实的依据是：由董事会选举产生的市政委员会得到了地产主的认可。由于缺乏账目记录，我们无法得知是否有人向领事提出过抗议；该领事曾因财务管理不善对董事们处以500法郎的罚款，甚至将他们监禁，尽管据一位实际居住于此且听闻此事的居民告诉我们，监禁时间仅为半小时。

麦克莱伦（MacLellan）先生在其《上海史》中叙述道：“布伦尼埃·德·蒙莫朗子爵（Viscount Brenier de Montmorand），即总领事，为其行动辩护所依据的理由如下：‘由领事当局任命的董事会，亦可由同一当局解散。董事会篡夺了仅属于领事的权利。它在总领事馆以外的地点召集地产主开会。它对租界的事务管理不善。’关于最后这项指控，据说董事会犯下了相当严重的错误，它阻止了副知县的调查，并按照一名负责外滩事务的英国建筑师所否决的方案开始修建外滩。该外滩随后坍塌。然而，大多数人认为，这场争执更多是双方情绪激化的结果，而非原则性问题。据说，英租界社群普遍倾向于支持领事馆的观点。这一情况在某种程度上得到了以下事实的证实：在10月19日的会议上，一位英国地产主提议由领事行使任命新董事会的权利，而该提议未遭反对。布伦尼埃·德·蒙莫朗子爵在任命后来被他宣布解散的董事会时，只是效仿了其两位前任的做法，且如此任命的董事中无人提出反对。董事会认为其有权在不请示总领事的情况下召集地产主会议；而总领事则宣称此举违反了1781年3月的法律，该法律禁止居住在黎凡特和巴巴里港口的法国公民在未获得驻君士坦丁堡大使或各港口领事许可的情况下集会。他适用了这部法律，尽管该法律在1865年的中国是否适用颇存疑问。

III. The Crisis of 1865.
B.- Order of the French Consul General.
We, Consul General for France in Shanghai:
"Considering the order of Mr. Edan, one of our predecessors dated April 12, 1862 establishing that the Municipal Council of the French Concession in Shanghai, holds its rights only through the appointment of the Consulate General for France;
Considering the circular issued by the same Consul dated April 29, 1862 by which he informs Messrs Edward Schmidt, Eugenie Buissonnet, Hi Heynard, J. Maniquet and Fajard that he has appointed them members of the Municipal Council of the French Concession;
Considering the report of the general meeting of land owners dated April 30, 1864 duly signed and rendered legal wherein it was stated that the actual Council was equally appointed by Mr. Goleux, then acting Consul General for France, who at the said meeting suggested the land owners to approve the choice he had made;
Whereas all members of the Municipal Council, far from protesting at the time against this sort of nomination, had accepted it by letters of thanks, a few of which kept in the registry of this Consulate General, prove their absolute compliance;
Whereas in each and every case, there have been written protests on their part in the registry of this Consulate at the period of their nomination.
Considering the instructions given, unknown to us, on the 2nd of this month by the Municipal Council to the Chief of French Police whereby it arrogates to itself rights which do not belong to it and which would compromise our good relations with the local authorities or the public safety.
Considering our letter dated October 4 by which we invited the Municipal Council to revoke a part of the said instructions, after having come to an arrangement with us for mutual understanding.
Whereas the Municipal Council did not even deign to reply to this letter:
Considering the advertisement of the Municipal Council inserted in the local Press this day, whereby it summons the land owners to meet at a place other than the French General Consulate where such meetings have always been held.
Whereas in this summoning land owners, unknown to us, without having previously arranged it with us, the Municipal Council has acted not only contrary to all precedents, but placed itself under the scope of article 86 of the law of March 1781, applicable to China and which forbids every kind of meeting held without the authorization of His Majesty's Consul.
Considering moreover that the Municipal Council has on several occasions gone beyond its rights, particularly in mortgaging the property of the Community without having previously obtained the assent of the land owners.
Considering, besides, that not only is the Municipal Council not composed of a sufficient number of members present, but, above all several of the members actually in Shanghai are absent during a large portion of the year, in such a manner that it frequently happens that only two members viz: Messrs. 鉴于市政委员会全体成员当时不仅未对这种提名方式提出抗议，反而通过感谢信予以接受，其中几封保留在本总领事馆登记处的信件证明了他们的完全顺从；

鉴于市政委员会今日在当地报刊上刊登的广告，据此广告，它召唤地产主在法国总领事馆以外的地点开会，而此类会议以往均在总领事馆举行。

From the Echo de Chine of January 30, 1923.

The Crisis of 1865.
One will have noted the important difference which exists between the Municipal Commission instituted by the Consul and the former Council: whilst the latter was composed of five Frenchmen only, we now find ourselves face to face with a Commission composed of thirteen members, six of whom, at least, judging by their names, are foreigners. One may be allowed to ask if already at that time the Consul had received, if not the definite text, at least the general basis of the Municipal regulations approved of by the Department of Foreign Affairs and which would have foreseen the composition of a Mixed Council, formed partly of French citizens and partly of foreigners. We are tempted to believe so, because one could not explain how a Consul could have, of his own authority, so quickly departed from the exclusively French policy of his predecessors.

We may easily imagine the noise this affair caused in both Concessions, but chiefly in French circles. Mr. Buissonnet, who left for France after this incident and who had to return in 1868 or 1869 remarks that the crisis had not yet passed. He writes: "Shanghai does not at all resemble the town it was when I left it about three years ago, and I would be greatly disappointed if I had to again to make my residence there. Firstly a large number of my friends have left and those who still remain there have not maintained amongst themselves the intimate relations which had rendered a sojourn in that town bearable... Sad to relate that the little French Community formerly remarkably well united, is at present even more divided than the whole European population put together: this had come about above all through the discussions which had been aroused by the regrettable Consular and Municipal struggles which took place lately in this Concession, and on the subjects of which everyone unfortunately has ranged himself on one side or the other with a partiality which ought certainly to have been avoided".

"Elisée Reclus", writes Mr. Fauvel "makes reference to sovereign Consular rights when he says, in speaking of the British Concession: "It is there also that the majority of French residents had established themselves and also who escaped from the neighbouring noisy quarters of the old town or who desired to escape the discretionary power of their Consul, who was equipped with almost dictatory rights." He undoubtedly thought when writing these bitter lines of the famous decision of Brenier de Montmorand, Consul General, when he ordered the imprisonment of the entire body of the French Municipal Council until it had accepted the regulations which he had just decreed and which the Councillors had refused to sign. The reason for their arrest, such as it was given in official documents published at the time, is not precisely that, but we have given this extract to indicate the sensation that the incident caused. We do not however, think that this measure was meant to cause so many French people to move away from the Concession as said by Mr. Elisée Reclus. The real cause why so few French people, we should say few Europeans, resided on our side was because there were only a few European residences constructed, and it was this same reason moreover, which caused the French people to live in the International Settlement in 1865.

1865年的危机。
人们会注意到，由领事设立的市政委员会与之前的公董局之间存在重要差异：后者仅由五名法国人组成，而现在我们面对的是一个由十三名成员组成的委员会，其中至少六人，从姓名判断，是外国人。人们不禁要问，是否在那时，领事即使没有收到确切文本，至少也收到了外交部批准的市政规章的一般基础，而这些规章曾预见到一个由法国公民和外国人共同组成的混合公董局的构成。我们倾向于相信是这样，因为否则无法解释一位领事何以能凭一己之权，如此迅速地背离其前任 exclusively French（专属法国人）的政策。

我们可以轻易想象此事在两个租界，尤其是法国圈子里引起的轩然大波。布伊松内（Buissonnet）先生在此事件后前往法国，并于1868或1869年返回，他指出危机尚未过去。他写道：“上海与我大约三年前离开时的城市面貌截然不同，如果我不得不再次在那里居住，我会深感失望。首先，我的许多朋友已经离开，而那些仍然留在那里的人之间，也没有保持那种曾使在该城居住变得可以忍受的亲密关系……令人难过的是，以前团结得非常好的小法国社区，现在甚至比整个欧洲人口加起来还要分裂：这主要是由于最近在该租界发生的令人遗憾的领事与市政斗争所引发的讨论，不幸的是，每个人都带着本应避免的偏见站到了某一方。”

福韦尔（Fauvel）先生写道：“埃利塞·雷克吕斯（Elisée Reclus）在谈到英租界时提到了主权领事权利：‘那里也是大多数法国居民定居的地方，他们也是为了逃离老城附近嘈杂的区域，或是为了逃避其领事的专断权力，这位领事拥有近乎独裁的权利。’”他在写下这些尖刻的文字时，无疑想到了总领事布伦尼埃·德·蒙莫朗（Brenier de Montmorand）的那项著名决定，当时他下令将整个法租界公董局成员监禁，直到他们接受他刚刚颁布而议员们拒绝签署的规章为止。官方文件中给出的逮捕理由并非完全如此，但我们引用这段摘录是为了表明该事件引起的轰动。然而，我们并不认为这项措施意在导致如此多的法国人像埃利塞·雷克吕斯所说的那样搬离租界。如此少的法国人——我们应该说很少的欧洲人——居住在我们这边，真正的原因是因为建造的欧式住宅寥寥无几，而且也正是这个原因，导致法国人在1865年居住在国际公共租界。

At the general meeting of land owners held in the
French General Consulate in 1886 at the end of April,
Mr. Meynard, an old member of the Council, before the
opening of the meeting, made the following declaration
in the presence of the Assembly, which was presided over
by the Consul General: "Gentlemen, I am retiring. You will
understand that I cannot easily either approve or disap-
prove the reports presented to you by the temporary Com-
mission, owing to the fact that the first months of the
year were administered by the Council, of which I was Vice-
President and that on the occasion of the rendering of
reports for these six months, we were condemned , my col-
leagues and myself to pay a fine of 500 Francs under ar-
ticle 401 of the Penal Code (Chapter on robberies). I
can't, therefore, so long as this judgement is not amended,
consider myself as having a right to approve the manage-
ment of the dismissed Council".
This fine and the injurious qualification with which
he had been branded had greatly moved him as one could
understand; anyhow another question which occupied him
more was that concerning the rights of Municipal Council-
lors. For, after this preamble, he at once began an ad-
dress (of which we give a summary) in favour of more ex-
tensive powers being given the Municipal Council: "The
tax may only be voluntary. Nothing actually obliges the
ratepayers to pay taxes voted by a Council which they had
not selected. The present Municipal Council is not an au-
thority. The Concession can exist only on the condition
that the Cosmopolitan residents of this Concession are
free to choose their representatives and that the latter,
when their administrative actions infringe the law, be
responsible to them only". And throwing in defiance this
last phrase, "I reserve to myself the right to pay the
taxes voluntarily," he went out, followed by Mr. Laren,
Mr. Vialut and several other Frenchmen.
The General Assembly did not seem to have been much
moved by Mr. Meynard's speech: they quietly discussed the
examination of the reports. Then however, it came to the
question of passing them and to vote the budget for the
next year a certain Mr Hegg asked for explanations. "What
difference was there between the present situation and
that of a year ago? Was the present meeting valid or not?"
This was the question dwelt upon by many persons. Was it
necessary that two-thirds of land owners must be present?
Mr. Meynard had asserted that he would only pay taxes
voluntarily: could the land owners thus at their pleasure
refuse to pay taxes?
He was told that according to established custom
one-third of the land owners was sufficient to render va-
lid a general meeting and that as regards the refusal to
pay taxes, every rate payer was amenable on this point
to his Consul, before whom the question would be immediate-
ly brought in case of refusal.
Mr. Hegg insisted that "the Council must be elected
by the rate payers", and demanded that they await at least
the new regulations promised before, and sanction the
budget for the next year. He feared that the present Coun-
cillors, knowing that they would be so, but for a few
months only, would not be eager to spend the sums placed
at their disposal and consequently the land owners would
not yet have to vote for supplementary funds.
We thus found himself at a rather noisy discussion
at this meeting; eventually an understanding for a 16 months'
budget was reached and the following resolution was voted

在1886年4月底于法国总领事馆举行的地产所有人全体会议上，公董局老成员梅纳尔（Meynard）先生在会议开始前，在由总领事主持的大会面前发表了如下声明：“先生们，我要退出了。你们会理解，由于年初的几个月是由我担任副主席的公董局管理的，而在就这六个月的工作提交报告时，我和我的同事根据《刑法典》第401条（抢劫罪章节）被判处支付500法郎的罚款，因此我很难轻易批准或否决临时委员会向你们提交的报告。所以，只要这一判决未被修正，我就不能认为自己有权批准被解散公董局的管理工作。”
正如人们所能理解的那样，这笔罚款以及强加于他的侮辱性定性使他深受触动；无论如何，另一个更令他关切的问题是关于公董局议员的权利问题。因为，在这段开场白之后，他立即开始发表演讲（我们在此提供摘要），主张赋予公董局更广泛的权力：“税收只能是自愿的。实际上没有任何义务迫使纳税人支付由一个他们并未选出的公董局所投票决定的税款。目前的公董局不是一个权威机构。租界的存在只能基于这样一个条件：即租界内的国际居民可以自由选举他们的代表，且后者仅在行政行动违法时才对选民负责。”说完这最后一句挑衅的话，“我保留自愿纳税的权利”，他便走了出去，拉伦（Laren）先生、维亚吕（Vialut）先生和其他几位法国人跟随其后。
大会似乎并未因梅纳尔先生的演讲而受到太大震动：他们平静地讨论了审查报告的事宜。然而，随后到了通过报告和投票决定下一年度预算的问题时，一位名叫赫格（Hegg）的先生要求解释。“目前的局势与一年前有何不同？本次会议是否有效？”这是许多人深思的问题。是否必须有三分之二的地产所有人出席？梅纳尔先生已声称他只愿自愿纳税：那么地产所有人是否可以随意拒绝纳税？
他被告知，根据既定惯例，三分之一的地产所有人出席足以使全体会议有效；至于拒绝纳税的问题，每位纳税人在此问题上均受其领事管辖，一旦发生拒付情况，该问题将立即提交给领事处理。
赫格先生坚持认为“公董局必须由纳税人选举产生”，并要求至少等待此前承诺的新规章出台，然后再批准下一年度的预算。他担心目前的议员们明知自己任期仅剩几个月，便不会急于花费交由他们支配的款项，因此地产所有人还不需要投票表决追加资金。
于是，我们在会议上陷入了一场相当喧闹的讨论；最终，就为期16个月的预算达成了谅解，并投票通过了以下决议

19.

by a feeble majority: " As soon as the temporary Commission
ceases to exist no sum spent may be drawn out of the present
budget without the special sanction of the land owners and
if there be any balance in the hands of the Commission it will
be placed at the disposal of the land owners."
This resolution at least gave a right to the land
owners to make use of at their pleasure the sums placed by
them at the Council's disposal.

A month later the land owners met once more in General
Assembly and Mr. Brenier de Montmorand, the Consul, who pre-
sided by authority of his office, addressed them in the fol-
lowing terms which sufficiently explained the object of the
meeting: "I had hoped, Gentlemen, to be able to let you know
to-day of the new municipal organization in the French Con-
cession, but the importance of the questions which it raises,
has determined my Government to have it examined in all its
aspects by a Commission composed of specially competent per-
sons. However, the Commission not being able to finish the
work in due time I was requested to consider means securing
for three months more the services of this Commission.
I have already assured myself of the competency of the
temporary Commission and I trust that you will be quite wil-
ling to continue in your confidence towards it and extend its
powers for a little time more".
It will be noted that the Consul's tone is no longer
so sharp as that in his order; perhaps complaints had been
made against him at a high place; on the other hand, he cer-
tainly knew then that the new regulations gave the electors
of the Concession the right to elect their Council without
the Consul's interference in the selection of persons; it is
therefore not astonishing that the tone of his words differ
from that in his order and that he requests the land owners
to prolong the mandate of the temporary Commission.

These regulations of 1866 had to be modified again in
1868.
It was moreover stipulated at the end of the new re-
gulations, which were published in the "North China Herald"
of July 14, 1866 and sent by circular letter to all land
owners on July 19, 1866, that the Consul General had reserved
to himself the right, after consultation with the municipal
Commission as well as with principal members of the Community, to
bring into the present regulation, such changes as may appear
to him necessary in the interest of the Community and compa-
tible with his responsibility vis a vis his Government in
such matters.
The first municipal elections took place on Sunday,
the 2nd September, the following being elected: Messrs. Morel,
Bate, Besron, Lillet, Mounier, Whithall, Yates and Thirie.

The last regulations of 1866 with the exception of a
few modifications are those which are in force at the present
time. "The changes which were made in the first regulations
says Mr. Mao T'ollan "had reference to the requisite qualities
of the electors and to the article which dealt with the ar-
rest in the Concession of persons other than French, without
warrants issued by representatives of other Powers, without
the Consul General having signed them, or without the presence
of Police".
We have not yet given the actual text of these re-
gulations of 1866; they will come in their place better when
the new modification will be asked for, which would give the
Council more powers than it had before.

以微弱多数通过：“一旦临时委员会不复存在，未经土地所有者特别批准，不得从现行预算中支取任何款项；如果委员会手中尚有任何余额，将交由土地所有者支配。”
这项决议至少赋予了土地所有者随意使用由其交由公董局支配的款项的权利。

一个月后，土地所有者再次召开大会，领事 Brenier de Montmorand 先生依其职权主持会议，并向他们发表了如下讲话，充分说明了会议的目的：“诸位先生，我原本希望今天能向你们通报法租界新的市政组织情况，但鉴于其所提出的问题的重要性，我国政府已决定由一个由特别胜任的人员组成的委员会对其各个方面进行审查。然而，由于该委员会无法在规定时间内完成工作，我被要求考虑采取何种措施，以确保该委员会的服务再延续三个月。
我已经确认了临时委员会的能力，我相信你们会非常愿意继续信任它，并将其权力再延长一段时间”。
值得注意的是，领事的语气不再像他的命令中那样尖锐；也许有人向上级对他提出了投诉；另一方面，他当时肯定知道，新规章赋予租界选民选举公董局的权利，而领事在人选选择上不得干涉；因此，他的言辞语气与命令中的语气不同，并且他请求土地所有者延长临时委员会的任期，这也就不足为奇了。

这些 1866 年的规章不得不在 1868 年再次修改。
此外，在 1866 年 7 月 14 日刊登于《北华捷报》（North China Herald）并于 1866 年 7 月 19 日以通函形式发送给所有土地所有者的新规章末尾规定，总领事保留在与市政委员会以及社区主要成员协商后，为了社区的利益并与其对政府在此类事务上的责任相兼容，对现行规章进行他认为必要的更改的权利。
第一次市政选举于 9 月 2 日星期日举行，当选者如下：Morel、Bate、Besron、Lillet、Mounier、Whithall、Yates 和 Thirie 诸位先生。

除了少数修改外，1866 年的最后几项规章即是目前生效的规章。“对第一项规章所做的修改，” Mao T'ollan 先生说，“涉及选民的必要资格，以及关于在没有其他强国代表签发、未经总领事签署或没有警察在场的情况下逮捕租界内非法籍人士的条款。”
我们尚未提供这些 1866 年规章的实际文本；当要求给予公董局比此前更多权力的新修改时，它们将在更合适的位置出现。

From the Echo de Chine of January 31, 1925.

IV. Criticism and demands for modification.
The Republic was proclaimed in France on September
4, 1870.
From December 23, a certain Mr. Pollotin, represen-
tative of Messrs. Meynard, Cousin & Co. protested violent-
ly in a letter addressed to the Council, against the regu-
lations of the Concession. "Those regulations are the work
of a despotic Government and sanction the encroachment
of authority on the citizen's liberty; to-day when the
Republic has redressed the abuses of the Empire, it is
necessary to proceed with the least possible delay to the
revision of this authoritative order, to banish the anti-
liberal tendencies with which it abounds".
By virtue of these aristocratic articles the Conces-
sion finds itself entirely at the mercy of the Consul-Ge-
neral for France. To maintain the regulations would be to
expose the community to the coming of a new Consul less
conciliatory than the present one, brought over to a re-
gime of good pleasure".
To read these bombastic declarations one would be temp-
ted to believe that one is in the presence of those
brawlers who are to be found at any time, upon whom words
of freedom and the rights of citizens have an influence
like that of a spring box, which suddenly throws out a
little imp hidden therein. It is, however, more probable
that Mr. Pollotin, the representative of the Mr. Meynard,
who was imprisoned, as is known, in 1865, had acted es-
pecially under the influence of a remembrance of the charge
which overtook his patron.
Alas, it was then the period when vanquished France
was cruelly occupied, when Paris was besieged, when the
country struggled in vain, in desperate leaps under the
iron hand of German occupation. In Shanghai as well as in
France sorrow was in the heart, the resentment against an
Empire lacking foresight had specially given place to
fears for the invaded country. The Municipal Council rep-
lied to Mr. Polletin's letter with moderation and tact.
"The Municipal Council", it was said in the proposi-
tion made by Mr. Voisin and seconded by Mr. Morol, "admits
that the regulations governing the Concession require
modifications in a really liberal sense. It is, however,
of opinion that, considering the reduced number of its
members at present and especially owing to terrible dif-
ficulties which the French Government is endeavouring to
overcome, it would be preferable to wait until the next
municipal elections have taken place, and the peace made
would enable the Government to have the time to listen to
the appeal from Shanghai before the Council provokes or
encourages any steps towards the modification of the said
Regulations".

It does not seem that Mr. Allot, whose name will be
referred to many times in the course of this history, had
voted in favour of this reply; because it is simply said
that it was voted for. The Council then was composed of
4 members only including Mr. Aymari who certainly voted
in favour of Mr. Voisin's proposition.
We do not think we are mistaken in saying that one
of the greatest preoccupations which engrossed Mr. Allot's
brains was to bring forth the changes in the regulations
of 1869, because from June 13, 1872 Mr. Morol, the Chairman,

四、批评与修改要求。
法兰西共和国于 1870 年 9 月 4 日宣布成立。
自 12 月 23 日起，某位 Pollotin 先生，即 Meynard, Cousin & Co. 公司的代表，在一封致公董局的信中激烈抗议租界的规章。“这些规章是专制政府的产物，认可当局对公民自由的侵犯；如今共和国已纠正了帝国的弊政，必须尽可能迅速地修订这一权威性的命令，消除其中充斥的反自由倾向”。
根据这些贵族性质的条款，租界完全受制于法国总领事。维持这些规章将使社区面临迎来一位不如现任领事那么温和的新领事的危险，从而陷入一种随心所欲的体制”。
读到这些夸夸其谈的宣言，人们不禁会以为面对的是那些随时可见的莽汉，自由和公民权利的字眼对他们产生的影响就像弹簧盒一样，突然弹出其中隐藏的小鬼。然而，更有可能的是，Pollotin 先生作为 Meynard 先生的代表——众所周知，Meynard 先生于 1865 年被监禁——其行为主要是受到对其雇主遭遇指控的记忆的影响。
唉，那时正是战败的法国遭受残酷占领的时期，巴黎被围困，国家在德国占领的铁腕下徒劳地挣扎，做着绝望的跳跃。在上海以及在法国，悲痛萦绕心头，对缺乏远见的帝国的怨恨特别让位于对被入侵国家的担忧。公董局以克制和策略回复了 Polletin 先生的来信。
“公董局”，在 Voisin 先生提出并由 Morol 先生附议的提案中说道，“承认管理租界的规章确实需要按照真正自由的精神进行修改。然而，公董局认为，考虑到其目前成员人数减少，特别是鉴于法国政府正努力克服的可怕困难，最好等待下一次市政选举举行，且和平达成后，使政府有时间听取来自上海的呼吁，之后公董局再引发或鼓励采取任何修改上述规章的步骤”。

Allot 先生的名字在本历史叙述中将多次被提及，他似乎并未投票赞成这一回复；因为文中仅简单提到该回复获得通过。当时的公董局仅由 4 名成员组成，包括肯定投票赞成 Voisin 先生提案的 Aymari 先生。
我们认为这样说不会错：占据 Allot 先生头脑的最大关切之一，就是促成 1869 年规章的变更，因为从 1872 年 6 月 13 日起，主席 Morol 先生，

placed four plans of regulations on the table which had been
submitted to him by Mr. Millot.
Besides they had agreed to demand modifications. At the
General meeting of rate-payers, a very animated meeting which
took place on May 13, 1871 and the reading of which, by the
way would show that the rate-payers were taking an interest
(in the opposition at least) in the Council's management,
Mr. Emile Lepissier put forward directly the following ques-
tion to the Consul General. "Will not these regulations, which
place the Police in the Consul's hands be changed in the end?"
The Council of June 13 equally declares that it is im-
possible to postpone the modifications of the Municipal regu-
lations. "We all desire it very eagerly, says Mr. Voisin,
"and in this we are, but the voice of our mandatories: if we
have waited until to-day to occupy ourselves officially with
this, it is because circumstances had rendered the solution
neither probable nor even possible".
And at Mr. Morel's suggestion Mr. Voisin is officially
entrusted by the Council to place before it a plan to amend
the said regulations. The Council remarked that it would come
to an arrangement, after giving them its approval, with the
Consul General to bring them before the French Government.

It was on March 12, 1872 that Mr. Voisin reported to the
Council on the task which had been entrusted to him. After
drafting the regulation, which he submitted for the approval
of one of his colleagues, he ultimately came to the conclu-
sion that the "liberal tendencies which he had encountered
at the French Charge d'Affaires in Peking and at the Consul
General at Shanghai cannot be really efficacious unless a
meeting of electors expressed a wish on the subject". The
Municipal Council, says he "is in fact nothing but a simple
administrative Council and has no constituent or legislative
power whatever. It cannot borrow strength except by inter-
preting the expressed desires of rate-payers".
These modifications aimed first of all at the relations
between the Council and the Consul; they were "already sanc-
tioned by reason and almost appropriated by custom", says Mr.
Voisin. But the great point which meets with opposition from
the Councillors and the rate-payers is particularly the pay-
ment of the Police.
"It is undoubted:, says Mr. Voisin, "that the Consul
General, invested with judicial powers, requires to have at
his orders a body of police agents to enforce the execution
of judicial mandates; but is it rational or admissible that
the French Government should impose upon the Municipality a
charge which its financial resources do not permit it to bear?
Thirty eight and a half percent of the municipal revenues
are deducted to pay the so-called municipal Police: it is on
this question that the Council has a right to act. It can-
not but recommend to the meeting of electors organic changes
in the existence of the Municipality, but at least so long as
it is the administrator of public funds it cannot encourage
or maintain the existence of an expenditure so disproportio-
nate".
The Consul Mejan hastened to protest against this qualifi-
cation of the judiciary police given to the Police: "the Con-
sul" says he has no judicial police and this qualification
cannot be regarded as a part of Police duties which consist
in arresting Chinese offenders and in conducting them before
the Mixed Court to be judged.

Judging from what we have seen, it seems that it was at
the end of the public meeting on June 11, 1872 when the Mu-

将 Millot 先生提交给他的四份规章草案摆在了桌面上。
此外，他们已同意要求修改。在 1871 年 5 月 13 日举行的纳税人大会上——这是一次气氛热烈的会议，其记录显示纳税人对公董局的管理感兴趣（至少是在反对方面）——Emile Lepissier 先生直接向总领事提出了以下问题：“这些将警察置于领事手中的规章，最终难道不会被改变吗？”
6 月 13 日的公董局同样声明，推迟修改市政规章是不可能的。“我们都迫切希望如此，” Voisin 先生说，“在这方面，我们只是遵循委托人的意愿：如果我们直到今天才正式着手处理此事，那是因为局势使得解决方案既不可能，甚至也不具备可能性”。
并在 Morel 先生的建议下，公董局正式委托 Voisin 先生向其提交一份修正上述规章的计划。公董局指出，在获得批准后，将与总领事达成协议，将其提交给法国政府。

1872 年 3 月 12 日，Voisin 先生向公董局汇报了他受托完成的任务。在起草规章并提交给一位同事批准后，他最终得出结论：“他在北京法国代办和上海总领事处遇到的‘自由倾向’，除非选民会议就此表达愿望，否则无法真正生效”。他说，市政公董局“实际上只是一个简单的行政委员会，没有任何制宪或立法权。它只能通过诠释纳税人的明确意愿来获得力量”。
这些修改首先针对公董局与领事之间的关系；Voisin 先生说，这些关系“已得到理性的认可，并几乎被习俗所采纳”。但是，引起议员和纳税人反对的关键点特别是警察经费的支付问题。
“毫无疑问，” Voisin 先生说，“拥有司法权力的总领事需要有一队警察特工听命于他，以执行司法令状；但是，法国政府强加给市政当局一项其财政资源无法承担的负担，这合理或可接受吗？市政收入的百分之三十八点五被扣除用于支付所谓的市政警察：正是在这个问题上，公董局有权采取行动。它虽然不能建议选民会议对市政的存在进行有机变革，但至少只要它是公共资金的管理者，它就不能鼓励或维持如此不成比例的开支存在”。
Mejan 领事迅速抗议这种赋予警察的“司法警察”称谓：“领事”他说，“没有司法警察，这种称谓不能被视为警察职责的一部分，警察的职责在于逮捕中国罪犯并将其引渡至混合法庭受审”。

根据我们所见，似乎是在 1872 年 6 月 11 日的公开会议结束时，当市

nicipal Council presented its reports to the General meeting
of rate-payers, that the question of the modifications to be
introduced in the regulations were to be decided. It is as-
serted with no little surprise that the question was not even
brought forward and that at the meeting there was but one
rate-payer present, Mr. Baron who appeared to be rather em-
barrassed: "Being unable, says he, either to discuss or to
vote for others he asked if the Council could vote definite-
ly in the absence of a majority of rate-payers.
He was told that first of all if the rate-payers were
not coming, it must probably be because they had no observa-
tions to make; if, in the neighbouring Concession the rate-
payers could vote for their budget, it was not the same in
the French Concession: "Here, it is the Council that votes
the budget and there is no question either of the right of
rate-payers to discuss the budget or of the obligation to
convene them in public meeting. If they are requested to at-
tend a General meeting it is through the courtesy of the
Council".
One would be tempted to believe at this distance and
without knowing in what tones these observations were made--
to judge by the latter part of the meeting, the tone may
have been rather sharp -- that the Council was voluntarily
assuming in its turn a dictatorial attitude.
Whatever it may be, it is interesting to learn that the
electors were absent and that no body spoke any more about
the modifications to be made in the Regulations.

During the whole of 1872 no mention of it whatever was
made and the question seems to have been buried. It is true,
that from the beginning of the year, we no longer see the in
Council, the name of Mr. Villot, who was an ardent defender
of the new regulations. He must have probably returned to
France. No rate-payer attended the General meeting of June
25, 1873. A peculiar feature must here be noted: this general
meeting had always until then been held under the chairmanship
of the Consul General. This year, at the Consul's own
request, the latter being then Mr. Godeux, it was held under
the chairmanship of the Council.

During the year 1874, Mr. Villot re-appeared amongst the
Councillors. No allusion was however made during that year
to modifications to be brought into the regulations, but our
readers know that the year 1874 was marked by the grave af-
fair of the Virgo Guild. On May 3 a crowd of rioters held
the Eastern part of the Concession, attacked the foreigners,
commenced to set fire to the houses of Europeans and procee-
ded as far as the Municipal Hall. The Council and the Consul
were far from having an understanding with each other in
this matter and the meetings of the second half year were
all devoted to exonerating the Council of all responsibili-
ty for this riot.
The year '875 was above all marked by the discussions
between the Municipal Council (?) and the French Municipal
Council on the subject of the construction of bridges over
the Yankingpang.
At the end of the year, however, the Council again found
itself in disagreement with the Consul on the subject of the
Police. The Council demanded that all candidates for the po-
lice force should serve a probationary period of six months
before being definitely incorporated unless they could produce
to the Consul a municipal doctor's certificate which is com-
pletely satisfactory.
The acting Consul, Mr. de Charpedollaine, wrote to the
Council to inform it that "he could not abandon any part of

市政委员会向纳税人大会提交报告时，本应决定拟对章程进行的修改事宜。令人颇为惊讶的是，该问题甚至未被提出，且出席会议的纳税人仅有一位，即巴伦男爵（Baron），他似乎显得相当尴尬：“他说，由于既无法代表他人讨论，也无法代表他人投票，他询问委员会在缺乏多数纳税人的情况下，是否仍可进行有效表决。”
他得到的答复是，首先，如果纳税人不来，大概是因为他们没有什么意见要发表；其次，在邻近的租界，纳税人可以对其预算进行投票，但在法租界情况并非如此：“在这里，由工部局对预算进行表决，既不存在纳税人讨论预算的权利问题，也不存在召开公开会议召集他们的义务。如果他们被要求参加全体大会，那是出于工部局的礼遇。”
人们不禁会认为——鉴于当时距离现在已远，且不知这些言论是以何种语气说出的——从会议后半部分的情况判断，语气可能相当尖锐——工部局此时自愿采取了一种独裁的态度。
无论如何，有趣的是，选民缺席了，且再无人提及拟对章程进行的修改。

在整个1872年期间，对此只字未提，该问题似乎已被搁置。确实，从年初开始，我们在工部局成员中再也看不到维洛特先生（Mr. Villot）的名字，他是新章程的热情捍卫者。他大概已经返回法国。1873年6月25日的全体大会没有一名纳税人出席。此处需注意一个特殊现象：在此之前，全体大会一直由总领事主持。这一年，应时任总领事戈杜克斯先生（Mr. Godeux）本人的请求，大会改由工部局主持。

1874年期间，维洛特先生再次出现在董事名单中。然而，那一年并未提及要对章程进行修改，但读者们知道，1874年的标志事件是严重的“处女行”（Virgo Guild）事件。5月3日，一群暴徒占据了租界东部，袭击外国人，开始焚烧欧洲人的房屋，并一直推进到工部局大楼。在此事上，工部局与总领事之间远未达成一致，下半年的会议全部致力于免除工部局对此次骚乱的任何责任。
1875年主要以工部局（？）与法国市议会关于在洋泾浜（Yankingpang）上建造桥梁的讨论为标志。
然而，在年底，工部局再次就警务问题与总领事发生分歧。工部局要求，所有警队候选人在正式录用前必须经过六个月的试用期，除非他们能向总领事提供一份完全令人满意的市政医生证明。
代理总领事德·夏尔佩多莱恩先生（Mr. de Charpedollaine）致函工部局，告知其“未经外交部长授权，他不能放弃

IV. Criticism and demands for Modification.
In 1876, the attacks recommenced.
At the General meeting of October 10, 1876, the Council was called upon to give the sense of the reply to be made to two letters from the French Consul General, one transmitting the copy of a petition from a certain number of voters demanding the convocation of a general meeting to express their views on diverse modifications which they purpose to make in the regulations of the Municipal organization; and in the other, he (the Consul) makes known his intentions, in case a general meeting of the electoral body is held. The Council at first intended to observe to the Consul General that the number of signatures on this petition, inscribed on the electoral list, did not represent the majority of electors and to leave it to the Vice-Chairman to explain to him the other considerations which went to form the views of the Council.
What were these modifications? The report of the meeting of October 10 does not give them: one finds, them, however, later in the discussions of 1882. Here is a summary:- The electors, to the number of 75, says Mr. Chapsal. 105 affirms Mr. Millot, who says he went himself to present the petition to the electors who demanded:
1) That new elections be held when the number of Municipal councillors will be in fact reduced by half.
2) That a councillor departing for Europe be considered as having resigned, and that he can not be permitted, in future, to regard himself, theoretically, as one of the members of the Municipality.
3) That two persons belonging to the same Commercial house, no matter what their positions may be, chief or employee, may not at the same time be members of the Municipal Council.
4) That members of the Municipal Council may not take part in deliberations in which they are directly interested, whether in their own name, or as mandataries".
We will examine the reasons which have caused the demand for these changes.
Foreign Representation.- In 1876 misunderstandings arose over the subject of an interpretation of the commercial tax. Here is the sequel to this affair, according to an account which one has rather erroneously made in the accounts of the meetings of September 7 and 8, 1876: " As none of the Councillors have spoken, none understanding sufficiently the English and French languages, and on the other hand, as the Secretary is equally incapable of translating the opinions which would be expressed in the course of the meeting, Mr. Maigman demanded that Mr. Taylor, an assistant in the Secretariat, be authorised to act as interpreter. Mr. Maigman remarked that in the face of the material impossibility in which one would find himself when dealing seriously with the affairs of the Community, inasmuch as the discussions are always attended by mistakes and misunderstandings, it would appear that some method should be urgently devised by which to get out of a situation of which he had recently noted its practical inconveniences. He demanded therefore, that they proceed without delay to the nomination of a new Council of a sort that they would

四、批评与修改要求。
1876年，攻击重新开始。
在1876年10月10日的全体大会上，工部局被要求就如何回复法国总领事的两封信件表明态度，其中一封信转交了一定数量选民提交的请愿书副本，要求召开全体大会，以表达他们对拟对市政组织章程进行的各项修改的意见；在另一封信中，他（总领事）说明了如果举行选举人团全体大会，他的意图是什么。工部局起初打算向总领事指出，这份请愿书上签署的人数，即在选民名册上登记的人数，并不代表选民的多数，并让副主席向他解释构成工部局观点的其他考虑因素。
这些修改是什么？10月10日的会议报告并未列出：然而，我们在后来1882年的讨论中找到了它们。以下是摘要：——沙普萨尔先生（Mr. Chapsal）称选民人数为75人。米约先生（Mr. Millot）则坚称为105人，他说他亲自向那些要求以下内容的选民提交了请愿书：
1) 当市政董事人数实际上减少一半时，应举行新的选举。
2) 前往欧洲的董事应被视为已辞职，且今后不得允许其在理论上仍将自己视为市政机构成员之一。
3) 属于同一家商行的两人，无论其职位是主管还是雇员，不得同时担任市政董事会成员。
4) 市政董事会成员不得参与与其有直接利害关系的审议，无论是以其个人名义还是以代理人身份”。
我们将审视导致提出这些变更要求的原因。
外籍代表权问题。——1876年，因对商业税的解释产生了误解。以下是此事的后续，根据对1876年9月7日和8日会议记录的相当错误的叙述：“由于没有任何一位董事发言，没有人能充分理解英语和法语，另一方面，由于秘书同样无法翻译会议过程中表达的意见，梅格曼先生（Mr. Maigman）要求授权秘书处助理泰勒先生（Mr. Taylor）担任口译员。梅格曼先生指出，面对在处理社区事务时将遇到的实际不可能性，因为讨论总是伴随着错误和误解，似乎亟需制定某种方法来摆脱他最近注意到其实际不便的这种局面。因此，他要求立即着手提名一个新的董事会，以便

have a President and Vice-President who could speak the two
languages". The meeting could not agree: the foreign Coun-
cillors insisted that the revival of the Council take place
in January next, and that the two French Councillors with
Mr. Bade, hand in their resignations and retire. Indeed, the
councils which followed were presided over by foreigners only
Messrs Hitch, Lang and Rice.
    Mr. Millot in his "Reponse" gives another version of the
incident: It was a question of languages and more or less of
the faithful translation of documents or of discussions, but
it was a rather important material question which affected
directly certain Councillors. He says: "In September 1876 the
Council was composed only of two French men, Messrs. Haignan
and Millot and four foreigners, Mr. Bade, Mr. Hitch, a part-
ner of the house of Russel, Mr. Lang, one of the heads of the
house of Butterfield and Swire and Mr. Wheelock. (one would
seek in vain for the name of Wheelock in the official reports)
the name of Mr. Rice only appearing. The notes of Mr. Millot,
who was a member of the Council, are certainly sufficiently
precise to permit the detection of a mistake. It is believed
that the two names cover one and the same person).
    Mr. Millot continues: "It was a question of replying to
a demand by Messrs. Butterfield and Swire on the subject of
the construction of covered wharves before the estates they
hold on lease on the shore of the Whangpoo".
    Mr. Millot, as agent of Mr. Remi de Montigny; Mr. Lang,
as a partner in Butterfield; Mr. Hitch, as Director of the
Shanghai Steam Navigation Company; and lastly Mr. Bade, as
lessee to whom Mr. Remi de Montigny had ceded the right of
frontage for the period of the lease, were interested par-
ties in the debate.
    Three of the members, Messrs. Bade, Haignan and Millot,
proposed to their colleagues- the Council being incomplete -
the sending of their joint resignation which would permit the
electors to nominate a new Council for the special purpose of
deciding, in a more independent fashion, this grave question.
    Their suggestion not prevailing, these three members re-
tired and made a direct appeal to the Community.
    A 105 electors petitioned the Consul-General of France to
convene a general meeting in the terms of article 17 of the
Regulations. No result attended the petition. And why? Be-
cause Messrs. Hitch, Lang and Wheelock, being the only rep-
resentatives of the Council, entrenched themselves behind
the following clause of the Regulations, restrictive of the
rights of the Consul for a similar motive: "The Consul-Gene-
ral can, when he deems it necessary, and after consultation
with the Municipal Council, convene an extraordinary meeting
of electors".
    Messrs Hitch, Lang and Wheelock declare that there was
no need to obtain the opinion of the Community and one heard
no more of the petition".

    Messrs. Lang, Rice and Hitch directed the affairs of the
Concession until January 24, 1877, and the last session but
one was marked by a curious little incident: The Consul-Gene-
ral had expressed the intention of fixing the elections for
January 15. The Vice-President had a conversation with the Con-
sul and at the meeting he informed his colleagues that the
Consul General had abandoned his first idea and "that he was
prepared to put off the elections to January 24 if that date
appeared more convenient to the Council". The French Conces-
sion, the Consul and the Council appeared to be in the hands
of strangers!
    It is necessary to say that the ensuing elections on
January 31 changed completely the composition of the Council

    米约先生在其《答复》（Reponse）中给出了该事件的另一个版本：这涉及语言问题，以及文件或讨论翻译的忠实程度或多或少的问题，但这更是一个直接影响某些董事的重要实际问题。他说：“1876年9月，董事会仅由两名法国人组成，即海涅安先生（Haignan）和米约先生，以及四名外籍人士，巴德先生、罗素洋行合伙人希奇先生、宝顺洋行（Butterfield and Swire）负责人之一朗先生，以及惠洛克先生（Wheelock）。（在官方报告中徒劳地寻找惠洛克的名字，出现的只有赖斯先生的名字。作为董事会成员的米约先生的笔记肯定足够精确，足以发现这一错误。人们认为这两个名字指的是同一个人）。
    米约先生继续说道：“问题在于回复宝顺洋行关于在他们租赁的黄浦江岸边地产前建造有盖码头的要求”。
    米约先生作为雷米·德·蒙蒂尼先生（Remi de Montigny）的代理人；朗先生作为宝顺洋行的合伙人；希奇先生作为上海轮船公司（Shanghai Steam Navigation Company）的董事；最后，巴德先生作为承租人，雷米·德·蒙蒂尼先生已将租赁期内的临水权转让给他，他们都是辩论中的利害关系方。
    三名成员，即巴德先生、海涅安先生和米约先生，向他们的同事提议——鉴于董事会成员不全——联合辞职，这将使选民能够为了以更独立的方式裁决这一严重问题而提名一个新的董事会。
    由于他们的建议未被采纳，这三名成员退职并直接向社区呼吁。
    105名选民根据章程第17条的规定， petitioned 法国总领事召开全体大会。请愿未获结果。为什么？因为希奇先生、朗先生和惠洛克先生作为董事会的唯一代表，躲在章程中限制总领事因类似动机行使权利的条款后面：“总领事在认为必要时，并与市政委员会协商后，可召开选举人特别会议”。
    希奇先生、朗先生和惠洛克先生宣称无需征求社区意见，此后便不再有人提及该请愿书”。

    朗先生、赖斯先生和希奇先生管理租界事务直至1877年1月24日，倒数第二次会议以一个奇特的小插曲为标志：总领事曾表示打算将选举定在1月15日。副主席与总领事进行了交谈，并在会议上告知同事，总领事已放弃最初的想法，“如果该日期对董事会更方便，他准备将选举推迟至1月24日”。法租界、总领事和董事会似乎都掌握在陌生人手中！
    有必要指出，随后于1月31日举行的选举彻底改变了董事会的组成

Cauoy Forbes, A. Hennequin, Mr. Louvier, E. Millot and H.
Vinay: it will be noted that those names with the exception
of the first are all French. The Presidency was given to
Mr. Lowvior, and the Vice-Presidency to Mr. Hennequin. Mr.
Rice, however, still remained on the Council, his term not
having expired. The Council was therefore composed of seven
persons, of whom five were French. This was evidently a rep-
ly to the foreign administration which had prevailed during
the preceding months.

One could find no allusion made at the meetings of the
Council to the regulation of discussions which arose bet-
ween the Consul and the Council in 1875, reports on which
had been sent to Paris. In 1879 at the meeting of February
13 the Council, moved perhaps by a recollection of these
discussions or more probably by the view of new requirements
which were felt, wrote in the report of the proceedings
that "On the proposition of Mr. Buntschilli, (a Swiss) and
Mr. Millot, the Council names a Committee composed of four
members, of whom two are French, Messrs. Millot and Vinay,
and two foreigners, Messrs Bluntschili and Wheeley (Wheel-
ock ) who will take charge of the preparations of a scheme
for the revision of the Regulations of the Municipal orga-
nization of the French Concession". "These regulations",
states the report, "have not been modified since the year
1869 and not being any more in keeping with the actual re-
quirements of the Concession, the Council thinks it is ur-
gent to revise them in a manner approaching as near as pos-
sible to those in force in the concessions to the North of
the Yangtze River".

Let us open here a parenthesis to explain the point of
view of the Council. The gross difference existing between
the two Concessions lay evidently in the fact, that the
Municipal Council of the International Concession is com-
pletely independent in everything, regarding the internal
administration of the Concession. Public works, police, traf-
fic regulations, public health, etc. are all dealt with
with full authority, its decisions having the force of law
on the residents, and the Police enforce them. The Council-
lors, apart evidently from their submission to the general
laws, to which the subjects of all nations are amenable,
depend in no manner for the exercising of their functions
upon their Consuls, who can not recall them. The Council-
lors in the French Concession, on the contrary, are, in prin-
ciple, only a debating body, none of their resolutions
operating until it receives the sanction of the Consul -Ge-
neral. The Consul ought nevertheless to render executory
within eight days, all deliberations relative to the Budget
of municipal income and expenditure, to the collection of
municipal revenues, to the distribution of the taxes amongst
the rate payers, to demands for exemption or reduction of
taxes, to the methods of recovering taxes, to the acquisition
or disposal of municipal properties.

The Consul, can, by decision assigned and subject to
approval by the Minister to Peking, refuse to render exe-
cutory a resolution of the Municipal Council relative to
the opening of public roads and places, projects for cons-
truction of wharves, canals, markets etc., sanitation work,
maintenance of roads, appropriations for public utilities,
sewage, and all matters upon which the Consul calls upon
the Council to discuss.

The Consul-General is besides in charge of everything
relating to the maintenance of order in the Concession and
the Police are placed exclusively under his orders, although
paid by the Concession. Finally he has the right to suspend

在董事会会议上，人们找不到任何提及1875年领事与董事会之间产生的讨论及其监管情况的记录，相关报告已发送至巴黎。1879年2月13日的董事会会议，或许是出于对这些讨论的回忆，更可能是出于对新需求的考量，在会议记录中写道：“根据本茨希利（Buntschilli，瑞士人）先生和米约先生的提议，董事会任命一个由四名成员组成的委员会，其中两名法国人为米约先生和维奈先生，两名外国人为布伦奇利（Bluntschili）先生和惠利（Wheeley，即 Wheelock）先生，负责起草修订法租界市政组织章程的方案。”报告指出，“这些章程自1869年以来未曾修改，已不再符合租界的实际需求，董事会认为迫切需要根据尽可能接近长江以北各租界现行章程的方式进行修订。”

在此我们要插叙一段，以解释董事会的观点。两个租界之间的巨大差异显然在于，公共租界工部局在租界内部行政事务方面完全独立。公共工程、警务、交通法规、公共卫生等均由其全权处理，其决定对居民具有法律效力，并由警察执行。董事们除了显然需服从各国臣民均须遵守的一般法律外，在行使职能时完全不依赖于其领事，领事无权罢免他们。相反，法租界的董事原则上只是一个议事机构，其任何决议在获得总领事批准之前均不生效。然而，总领事应在八天内使所有涉及市政收支预算、市政收入征收、纳税人税额分配、免税或减税申请、税收追缴方法、市政财产购置或处置的审议结果成为可执行文件。

总领事可以通过一项需经驻北京公使批准的决断，拒绝执行董事会关于开辟公共道路和场所、码头、运河、市场等建设项目、卫生工程、道路维护、公用事业拨款、污水处理以及总领事要求董事会讨论的所有事项的决议。

此外，总领事负责维持租界秩序的一切事务，警察虽由租界支付薪饷，但 exclusively 受其指挥。最后，他有权暂停

the Municipal Council, but he must report immediately to
Peking. The period of the suspension may be three months:
in the meantime a Municipal Commission nominated directly by
the Consul will direct the affairs of the Municipality.
The difference between these two statutes is as much more
striking here as when applied in a similar town.
"Truth on this side of the Yangtse and error on the
other side", one could say at the time when the creek was in
existence. "Truth as far as the middle line of Avenue Edward
VII and error on the other side", one would say to-day. We
can imagine that on several occasions the Municipal Councillors
found themselves longing as much for the prerogatives of their
neighbours as for shaking off the reins which were restrain-
ing their action. It is not astonishing, therefore, to find
the Council in 1879 demanding that the prerogatives of the Coun-
cil be extended and be in accord with those enjoyed by the
International Municipal Council.
On March 25, 1879, the Council took cognizance of a plan
proposed by the Committee for the revision of the regulations
of the municipal organization; approved the alterations pro-
posed; and decided to submit them to the French high associa-
tion of the Minister for Foreign Affairs, praying him to give
his sanction to the modifications, which had become necessary.

At the meeting of April 16, 1879, at which were present
Viscount Brenier de Montmorand, French Minister to Peking,
and Mr. Patenôtre, Chargé d'Affaires, the Council handed to
the Consul a copy of the regulations which had been adopted
by the Council and requested him to forward them to the French
Minister for Foreign Affairs. The Council delegated its Pre-
sident, Mr. Millot, to lay before the Minister for Foreign
Affairs all the explanations necessary to obtain his assent
to the proposed modifications.
Better still, in case these explanations came to nothing,
the members of the Council charged the President "to bring
this question, in their name, before the Chamber of Deputies,
for they consider it to be of the highest interest for the
future and the prosperity of the Concession that these regu-
lations be revised in such manner that they will no longer
fetter the regular working of the various municipal services
which have for their sole object the protection of the private
and commercial interests in the Concession."
"Viscount Brenier de Montmorand and Mr. Patenôtre, who at-
tended the meeting," writes Mr. Millot in his "Report" "made
only some small objections to the modifications proposed, but
admitted them in principle.
If these modifications have not been submitted to the elec-
tors, it was because the Consul had deemed it convenient not
to place M. Lemaire, the provisional Consul, in the delicate
position of having to summon the electors, as Mr. Godeaux,
the incumbent, in the circumstances already narrated (the
incident of September, 1876) had not also complied with the
wish expressed by the Community.
The Council in demanding the alterations in the regula-
tions of the municipal organization of 1869, in co-operation
with Viscount Brenier de Montmorand, who had suggested them,
was only following tradition. Mr. Gallo and Mr. A. Voisin had
on two occasions been charged with this work.
From the month of June, 1879, the date of my arrival in
France, until January, 1880, I had numerous conferences with
Mr. Laurent, Director of Consulates, and with Count d-Arlot,
a sub-director, charged more specially with Far Eastern Af-
fairs.
The negotiations proved abortive and I had taken note on
January 27, 1880, of the text which the department had finally
